Frames read myself: 8/27 screen-shared Unit 1 vocab deck (13 slides, 54:50-74:58: as-salaamu calaykum; ahlan/ahla/ahlayn; ahlan wa sahlan/ahla wa sahla; marHaban/marHaba; ana; ismii; min; madiinat; askun; fii/bi; tasharafna; shukran; cafwan) - no slide exists for wa calaykum as-salaam or maca as-salaama; 8/25 is a frozen Canvas screen share during the alphabet overview (board not visible); 9/1 room camera shows the whiteboard (باء تاء ثاء, أ إ ء, ب+ا+ب=باب, واو, ت+و+ت=توت, ت+و+ب+و+ا, 'Harf'); 9/3 camera shows the board briefly (yaa lesson) then her and the projector (Lingco drills, short-vowel tables). Spellings: her slides/board first, then Lingco vault, then the 9/5 answer-key drill spellings, then standard MSA (flagged own-knowledge). Every word from the 9/5 audit is re-listed (new_vs_0905:false) with fresh utterance spans; 33 entries are new (new_vs_0905:true). letters.notes: alif (8/27): long aa; connects only to the RIGHT (two shapes: ا / ـا); 'like a straight line'; always the tallest letter (taller than the tooth, 9/1). Coaching 9/3: if a reader sounds like 'e' that's accent - alif is a.

letters.notes: baa (8/27): 'very close to English b'; connects both sides - four forms; the tooth must be straight (90 degrees), not curved (a curved tooth becomes nuun); dot under the tooth. Name spelled باء (9/1). Short-vowel drill 9/3: ba, bu, bi, b.

her_clear_utterances.context: letter name baa' (with the final hamza)

letters.notes: taa (9/1): same shape as baa, TWO dots ABOVE; in handwriting she writes the two dots as a dash. Name spelled تاء. 9/3 drill: ta, tu, ti, t.
thaa (9/1): same shape, THREE dots above; fast handwriting uses a caret (^) for the three dots. The 'th' of three (not of 'the' - that is dhaal). Name spelled ثاء.

her_clear_utterances.context: 8/25 th sound ('thaa, th as in three')

letters.notes: waaw (9/1): connects only to the right (two shapes); first taught as the long vowel uu; she darkens the loop so it can't be read as miim (her habit, not a rule); she writes it all above the line, the book dips below - both fine, and connected it must dip. Consonant w comes in Unit 3.

yaa (9/3): third long vowel ii; two dots BELOW (or a dash); the independent/final tail is CURVY and dips BELOW the line (unlike the straight tooth of baa/taa/thaa); initial/medial yaa = baa with two dots under. Name yaa / yaa'.

letters.notes: hamza (8/27, 9/1, 9/3): the glottal stop; can't start a word alone - sits on alif (أ above for a/u, إ below for i); can sit on the line by itself mid/end of a word (jaa'a); never on the definite article al-. Not the name Hamza.
jiim (8/25 overview): 'j, or g - varies by region; Egyptians say g (from Coptic)'. Unit 3 letter.
Haa (8/25, 8/27): capital H - 'the sound is coming from here, I'm making some contraction in here: Haa, not haa'. Unit 3 letter; in marHaba, Harf, fuSHa, HaDratuka.
khaa (8/25): 'like my name Khouri - as if you're clearing your throat'. Unit 3 letter.
daal (8/25, 8/27, 9/1): plain d as in dip; like alif it does NOT connect to the left (8/27); taller than the tooth, shorter than alif (9/1). Unit 4 letter.
